target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students learning Linear Algebra

outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students learning Linear Algebra

sections.title: Introduction: The Quest of Vector Vic
sections.content: Introduce a character, 'Vector Vic' the robot, who needs to reach a specific target (Vector B) using only two fixed power paths (Vectors V1 and V2). The problem is framed as: How many units of V1 and V2 does Vic need? This sets up the linear system Ax = b.
sections.example: Vic stands at (0,0). V1 is a path going 2 units right, 1 unit up. V2 is 1 unit right, 3 units up. The target B is at (7, 11). How many V1s and V2s reach B?

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Determinant as Area
sections.content: Before solving the puzzle, we define the determinant. Visually demonstrate that the determinant of a 2x2 matrix is the signed area of the parallelogram formed by its column vectors. If the vectors are 'squished' together, the area is zero (no solution).
sections.example: Show a blue vector (2,1) and a red vector (1,3). Animate a yellow parallelogram forming between them. The determinant (2*3 - 1*1 = 5) represents the area of this shape.

sections.title: The Vector Combination Problem
sections.content: Show that finding the solution (x, y) means stretching V1 by 'x' and V2 by 'y' so they sum up to B. This creates a transformation where the unit square is stretched into the parallelogram we just saw. This sets the stage for Cramer's insight: area ratios.
sections.example: Animate the 'Recipe': x * [2, 1] + y * [1, 3] = [7, 11]. The grid deforms, showing how B lands somewhere in the coordinate system of V1 and V2.

sections.title: The Geometric Trick: Replacing a Column
sections.content: Explain the core of Cramer's Rule: If we replace V1 with the target vector B, the area of the new parallelogram (B and V2) is exactly 'x' times the area of the original parallelogram (V1 and V2). This is because only the component of B along V1 contributes to the change in area relative to V2.
sections.example: Visually replace the blue vector (V1) with the green vector (B). Show the original parallelogram (Area = 5) and the new one formed by B and V2 (Area = 10). The ratio 10/5 gives us x = 2.

sections.title: Shearing and Scaling Logic
sections.content: Use a 'shearing' animation to show why this works. Since B = xV1 + yV2, when we take the determinant of (B, V2), the 'yV2' part doesn't add any area because it's parallel to V2. We are left with the determinant of (xV1, V2), which is just x * det(V1, V2).
sections.example: Animate the parallelogram formed by (xV1 + yV2) and V2. Show the 'yV2' component sliding along V2 like a deck of cards (shearing), which doesn't change the area, leaving only the 'xV1' contribution.

sections.title: The Formula and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize Cramer's Rule as a ratio of areas. X is the area of the 'modified' parallelogram divided by the 'original' area. Generalize this to Y by replacing the second column. Conclude by solving Vector Vic's original problem.
sections.example: Final calculation display: x = det(B, V2) / det(V1, V2) = 10 / 5 = 2. y = det(V1, B) / det(V1, V2) = 15 / 5 = 3. Vector Vic needs 2 units of path V1 and 3 units of path V2!

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Quest of Vector Vic
lecture_lines: Meet Vector Vic, a robot with a mission.
He must reach target vector B using paths V1, V2.
How many units of each path does Vic need?
animations: A white circle #FFFFFF labeled 'V' representing Vic appears at the origin.
Blue arrow V1 #0000FF and red arrow V2 #FF0000 extend from the origin.
A green arrow B #00FF00 pointing to (7, 11) appears as the target.
Two blue V1 arrows and three red V2 arrows align tip-to-tail to reach B.
White text 'x V1 + y V2 = B' appears at the top, with 'x' and 'y' in yellow #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Determinant as Area
lecture_lines: The determinant represents the area of a parallelogram.
V1 and V2 form this area in our grid.
A zero area means no solution is possible.
animations: Blue vector V1 #0000FF and red vector V2 #FF0000 are shown on a black background.
A yellow parallelogram #FFFF00 at 0.3 opacity forms between V1 and V2.
The area of the parallelogram is labeled 'Area = 5' in yellow #FFFF00.
The boundary vectors V1 and V2 flash white #FFFFFF simultaneously.
Text 'det(V1, V2) = 5' appears below the shape in white #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Vector Combination Problem
lecture_lines: Solution x and y scale our basis vectors.
We stretch V1 and V2 to reach target B.
Cramer's Rule solves this using area ratios.
animations: The background basis vectors i and j transform into V1 #0000FF and V2 #FF0000.
Target vector B #00FF00 is highlighted at its position relative to the V1-V2 basis.
Coordinates '(2, 3)' appear next to the tip of B in yellow #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: The Geometric Trick: Replacing a Column
lecture_lines: Replace the first path, V1, with target B.
Form a new parallelogram with B and V2.
This new area is exactly x times the original.
Comparing these areas reveals our unknown value, x.
Area ratios provide a geometric bridge to algebra.
animations: Show the original yellow parallelogram #FFFF00 with area labeled '5'.
The blue vector V1 is removed and replaced by the green vector B #00FF00.
A new green parallelogram #00FF00 forms using B and V2 (red).
The new area is calculated and labeled 'Area = 10' in green #00FF00.
The expression 'x = 10 / 5' appears in white #FFFFFF, then simplifies to 'x = 2'.

storyboard.title: Shearing and Scaling Logic
lecture_lines: Why does replacing the column work so perfectly?
Target B consists of components xV1 and yV2.
The yV2 component shears the shape, preserving area.
Only the xV1 component contributes to the new area.
This leaves us with x times the original determinant.
animations: Vector B #00FF00 is shown as the vector sum of x*V1 and y*V2 components.
The y*V2 component of the parallelogram (B, V2) slides (shears) along the direction of V2.
A visual indicator shows that the height and base relative to V2 remain unchanged, preserving area.

storyboard.title: The Formula and Conclusion
lecture_lines: To find x, divide modified area by original area.
To find y, replace V2 with B and divide.
For Vic, x is 10 divided by 5, which is 2.
And y is 15 divided by 5, which is 3.
Vic reaches his goal with 2 V1s and 3 V2s!
animations: A general mathematical formula for x and y using determinants appears in white #FFFFFF.
Calculation 'y = 15 / 5 = 3' is displayed in red #FF0000 to match the V2 substitution.
Vic moves along the calculated path (2*V1 then 3*V2) to reach the target B.
